editorial:
Ever wonder why other countries seem to have their lives more put together than we do in the States? That is exactly what Michael Moore asks in this funny and eye-opening trip around the world. Instead of invading countries for oil or power, he decides to invade them to steal their best ideas. You get to tag along as he visits places like Italy, Finland, and Canada to see why their workers are happier and their schools are better. The vibe is lighthearted and curious, making it feel less like a boring history lesson and more like a road trip with a guy who loves to ask awkward questions.

What really works here is the pacing; it moves quickly from one country to the next so you never get bored. You will love seeing the shocked faces of people when he tells them how bad things are in America. While some people might find his style a bit too pushy, the points he makes about paid vacation and free college are hard to ignore. It is a great pick for anyone who likes to think about the world while having a good laugh.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a call to action for the American people. After seeing all the great perks other countries have, like better healthcare and shorter work weeks, Moore argues that these things are possible for us too. He ends by saying that the US does not need to be afraid of change. He encourages you to demand a better life for yourself and your family, leaving you feeling hopeful that things can improve.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves learning about the world and likes a bit of political humor.
